config.title: Build memoization utility with cache size limit

intro.title: Build memoization utility with cache size limit
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a memoization utility function that caches the results of expensive function calls to improve performance. You will learn how to implement a cache with a size limit, ensuring it doesn't grow indefinitely by removing the least recently used entries. The core programming concepts used include closures, higher-order functions, and basic data structures like objects or maps. You'll work with JavaScript constructs such as functions, objects, and conditional logic to create a practical, reusable tool.
intro.usecase: This memoization pattern is essential in performance-critical UI components like data dashboards and financial charts, where expensive calculations—such as aggregating metrics or transforming datasets—are repeated during user interactions like filtering or resizing. For example, a real-time analytics dashboard might recalculate summary statistics every time a user adjusts a date-range slider; a memoized utility with a cache limit ensures these computations are fast and memory-efficient, preventing slowdowns as users explore data. Developers implement this to maintain responsive interfaces in complex applications, balancing speed with controlled memory usage across sessions.

objectives: Implement a memoization function that caches computed results
Construct a cache object with size tracking and key-value storage
Configure cache eviction logic when the size limit is exceeded
Integrate argument serialization to generate consistent cache keys
Manipulate cache entries to maintain the most recently used items
Initialize the memoization utility with configurable size limits
Apply the memoized function to optimize repeated calculations

steps.title: Create the memoize function skeleton
steps.instruction: Create a function called memoize that takes another function as an argument and returns a new function.
steps.hint: Start with a function declaration or arrow function named memoize that accepts a single parameter (the function to memoize). Inside, return another function.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a memoize function skeleton that takes a function and returns a new function.
successCriteria: The code defines a function named memoize that accepts one parameter and returns another function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: You can return an arrow function or a regular function expression. The returned function should be able to receive arguments.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoize function now returns a new function that will later be used to check the cache and call the original function.
successCriteria: The memoize function returns a function that can accept arguments.

steps.instruction: Inside the returned function, create a cache key by joining all arguments with a separator (like a comma).
steps.hint: Use the arguments array and join them into a string. You can use the spread operator to get all arguments.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoized function will have a cache key created from its arguments.

steps.title: Check if result exists in cache
steps.instruction: Inside the memoized function, check if the cache object already has a value for the generated key. If it does, return that cached value immediately.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check if the key exists in the cache object. If it does, return the cached value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoized function will now check the cache before computing a new result, returning cached values when available.
successCriteria: The memoized function includes an if statement that checks if the cache object has the key, and returns the cached value when it exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're checking if the key exists in the cache object and returning the cached value when it does.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache lookup logic is missing or incorrect. You need to check if the cache object has the key and return the cached value when it exists.

steps.title: Compute and store new results
steps.instruction: Inside the returned function, after checking for cache misses, compute the result by calling the original function with the arguments, store it in the cache object using the key, and return it.
steps.hint: If the key is not in the cache, call fn(...args) to get the result, assign it to cache[key], then return that result.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoized function now handles cache misses by computing new values, storing them, and returning them.
successCriteria: The returned function includes code that calls fn(...args) when the key is not in cache, stores the result in cache[key], and returns the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling the original function with the arguments, storing the result in the cache object using the key, and returning it.

steps.title: Add cache size limit parameter
steps.instruction: Modify the memoize function to accept a second parameter named maxSize that specifies the maximum number of cache entries.
steps.hint: Add maxSize as a second parameter to the memoize function signature, right after the fn parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoize function will now accept a maxSize parameter, enabling cache size limitation in later steps.
successCriteria: The memoize function signature includes maxSize as a second parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added maxSize as a parameter to the memoize function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The memoize function should accept a second parameter named maxSize.

steps.title: Track cache keys in order
steps.instruction: Inside the memoize function, add an array variable called 'keyQueue' to track the order of cache key usage. Initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: You'll need this array to implement LRU (Least Recently Used) eviction later. Place it near your cache object.

// Similar: tracking order of items

successCriteria: A 'keyQueue' array variable is declared and initialized as an empty array inside the memoize function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared 'keyQueue' as an array inside the memoize function. It should be initialized as an empty array.

steps.title: Implement cache eviction logic
steps.instruction: Inside the memoized function, after computing and storing a new result, add logic to check if the cache size exceeds maxSize. If it does, remove the oldest key from both the cache object and the keyQueue array.
steps.hint: You can check if keyQueue.length > maxSize. If true, use shift() to remove the first element from keyQueue and delete that key from the cache object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoize function will now automatically remove the oldest cached entry when the cache size exceeds the specified limit, preventing unlimited memory growth.
successCriteria: The memoized function includes a check for cache size exceeding maxSize, and when it does, removes the oldest key from both cache and keyQueue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check if the cache size exceeds maxSize and remove the oldest key from both the cache object and keyQueue array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache eviction logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if keyQueue.length > maxSize and remove the oldest entry from both cache and keyQueue.

steps.title: Update key order on cache hits
steps.instruction: When a cached result is retrieved, move its key to the end of keyQueue to mark it as recently used. Add this logic inside the cache hit check.
steps.hint: When you find the key in cache, after returning the cached value, remove the key from its current position in keyQueue and push it to the end.
steps.expectedOutcome: The memoize function now properly tracks recently used cache entries by moving keys to the end of keyQueue when they are accessed.
successCriteria: Cache hits move the accessed key to the end of keyQueue using splice and push.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're removing the key from its current position in keyQueue and adding it to the end when a cache hit occurs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache hit logic needs to update keyQueue order. When a key is found in cache, remove it from keyQueue and push it to the end to mark it as recently used.
